flags.detail: The sole author, Dr. Ramavatar Singh Tyagi, is this journal's Managing Editor. COPE guidance on editors' own submissions (and the checks made by indexers such as DOAJ/UGC-CARE) expects such a paper to be handled by an independent editor with independent peer review and to carry a competing-interest statement. The manuscript has no competing-interest, funding or acknowledgement statement, and none was added. Suggested statement, to be used only if true: 'Dr. Ramavatar Singh Tyagi is the Managing Editor of International Research Insights: Multidisciplinary e-Journal. He was not involved in the editorial handling of, or the decision on, this article.' Note also that the issue's other nursing paper (Jaiprakash Tyagi, stress among B.Sc. Nursing students) comes from the same institution and uses the same template, and its author has the same surname. Two of the four papers in the founding issue are then linked to the editorial team, which reviewers of the journal may question.

Table 7 (level of patient-safety practice) in the source read Adequate 0 (0.0%), Moderate 2 (4.8%), Inadequate 17 (40.5%), Total 42 (100.0%). These rows add up to 19 students, not 42, and the Inadequate row is missing 23 students. The Interpretation, the Discussion, the Summary (former 'Result'), Table 8 (Practice: Inadequate 54.76%) and the author's own bar chart all give Adequate 2 (4.76%), Moderate 17 (40.48%), Inadequate 23 (54.76%), so the source table appears to have been shifted down by one row. The table was corrected to 2 / 4.76, 17 / 40.48, 23 / 54.76 (Total 42 / 100.0) to match. The author must confirm this correction before publication.

There are signs that an AI chatbot was used. Reference 4 ended with the chatbot reply 'Note: The author details in your original reference list combine two separate books. The correct APA 7 references are listed separately below.' (removed). The hyperlinks of references 8-10 carried '?utm_source=chatgpt.com' (removed). The chart images are default-style matplotlib output, and the text follows the same template as the issue's other nursing paper ('DISCUSSION ON ANALYSIS', 'Hence, the investigator felt the need to conduct the study entitled ...'). No copied web text or paraphrasing-tool 'tortured phrases' were found. Ask the author for an AI-use declaration and for written confirmation that every statement, number and reference has been checked (COPE/ICMJE position). Consider publishing an AI-use policy on the website.

(1) Several sources discussed in the text have no reference entry: Farokhzadian et al. (2024), cited twice by author-year; the WHO Multi-professional Patient Safety Curriculum Guide (described in six places: Need for the study and five literature sub-sections); 'A 2025 systematic review' of educational interventions; and 'A 2026 analysis of 30 cross-sectional studies from 13 countries'. (2) None of the 11 listed references is a study of patient safety among nursing students. The numeric citations ^1^-^11^ appear once each, in strict order, at points they do not support. Examples: ^4^ (a textbook) is attached to a finding of Farokhzadian et al.; ^5^ sits mid-sentence after 'planning'; ^6^, ^7^ and ^9^-^11^ are attached to the study's own results and summary (age distribution, demographic summary, data-collection statement). (3) Reference 4 conflates two books: the 11th-edition 'Nursing research: Generating and assessing evidence for nursing practice' (Wolters Kluwer, 2021) is by Polit & Beck, which is reference 6, and Wood & Ross-Kerr wrote reference 5. The chatbot note in the source said so. The author should add the missing references (Farokhzadian et al. 2024; WHO 2011 Multi-professional Patient Safety Curriculum Guide; the 2025 review; the 2026 analysis), cite each source where it is used, and replace or delete reference 4.

This is a study on human participants (students), but the only ethics statements are 'Permission was obtained from the concerned authority', 'Voluntary participation' and 'Confidentiality and anonymity were maintained'. No Institutional Ethics Committee approval is reported (no committee name, reference number or date; ICMR 2017 guidelines). Informed consent is not stated explicitly. Before publication, ask the author for the IEC approval details and a statement that written informed consent was obtained. The study was done at Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati, while the author's listed affiliation is J.S. University, Shikohabad. The author should also state his role at the study site; if the participants were his own students, that should be declared.

The methods are vague and contradict each other. Sampling technique: 'Consecutive Technique' in the Methodology list, 'As per study protocol' in the flow chart (Figure 1); the sample (42) appears to be the whole 2nd-semester class. Data collection tools: 'Self-administered questionnaire' and 'Interview schedule' (Data collection tools), 'Structured tools / checklist' (Figure 1), 'a knowledge questionnaire together with recorded skill and practice scores' (Research gap). The paper does not say how skills and practice were measured (observation checklist? self-report? existing records?). It gives no number of items, scoring or validity/reliability, and no data-collection period. The cut-offs for adequate/moderate/inadequate appear only on the charts (knowledge: 17-20 / 13-16 / 0-12 out of 20; skill and practice: 7-10 / 4-6 / 0-3 out of 10), not in the methods. The demographic variable 'previous clinical experience' is listed but never reported. Ask the author to clarify these points.

The paper keeps a thesis/proposal structure (Need for the study, Problem statement, Assumptions, Delimitation, Research gap, Need for the present study, plus a list and a flow chart for the same methodology). The text was kept, sections were reordered into the standard order, and headings were fixed. Points for the author: (1) the 'Conclusion' section ('Hence, the investigator felt the need to conduct the study entitled ...') is a proposal-style statement of need, not a conclusion; the real conclusions are in the 'Summary' (source 'RESULT'). Recommend merging Summary and Conclusion into one 'Conclusion' and moving or deleting the 'Hence ...' sentence. (2) The abstract's Results give no numbers; it should report N = 42 and the 88.10% / 59.52% / 54.76% findings and stay within 250 words. (3) There is no explicit 'Objectives' section; the 'Need for the present study' list reads like objectives. (4) The Discussion does not compare the findings with any other study (e.g. Farokhzadian et al. 2024). (5) The Summary largely repeats the Discussion. (6) There are no Limitations or Recommendations sections, although the flow chart ends with 'Conclusion & Recommendations'.

The manuscript gives no affiliation, e-mail or ORCID. The affiliation 'Vice Principal, Department of Nursing, J.S. University, Shikohabad, Uttar Pradesh, India' and the degree 'Ph.D. (Nursing)' were taken from the journal's editorial-board records. The author should confirm this is the correct affiliation for this work, or give his affiliation at the time of the study if he was then at Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati. A corresponding-author e-mail is needed for the first-page footnote and the website. There are no received/accepted dates (left empty), no data-availability statement and no acknowledgement/funding statement.

Minor inconsistencies, kept as in the source. (1) Delimitation: 'The study is delimited to government nursing colleges of Assam', but the study was done in one college only (Regional College of Nursing, Guwahati). (2) The study title varies: the article title; the problem statement ('... regarding patient safety in clinical practices among 2nd semester ...'); and the Conclusion ('Patient safety in clinical practices among B.Sc. Nursing Students of Regional College of Nursing ...'). (3) Rounding: Table 1 percentages add up to 100.1% and Table 6 to 99.99%, against stated totals of 100%. This is acceptable rounding. All counts add up to N = 42 in Tables 1-6, and every percentage matches its count (n/42).

References to verify. Ref 3, Basavanthappa, Nursing research (2nd ed., 2007): the issue's other nursing paper cites the same 2nd edition as 2014, so one year is wrong. Ref 11, MoHFW National Quality Assurance Standards for District Hospitals: no year (n.d.) and no URL. Ref 4 duplicates the title, edition, year and publisher of ref 6 (see the high citation flag). Refs 8-10 (WHO publications, item URLs) look genuine.

The 8 source charts were redrawn from the values printed on them, because image8 was only 976 px wide and the embedded titles 'Figure 1-4' clashed with the article numbering. The text-only flow chart was redrawn as Figure 1. Originals are kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-international-research-journal/55c29a40-3aee-5b96-9c75-9672107bc1f3/scratchpad/work_p3/orig_figs. Every table is also shown as a bar chart (Figures 2-9 repeat Tables 1-8), which adds about 3-4 printed pages. Most journals ask for either a table or a figure for the same data; consider keeping only the tables, or only Figure 9.

No sign of prior publication was found: no journal header, DOI, 'published in' note, volume/issue or old dates. The Word file was converted from a PDF (SolidFramework converter; PDF created 14 August 2026). As a routine step, ask the author for a declaration that the work is original and not under consideration elsewhere.
